newsitem.title: UK: UK wheat futures up, active on shipper buying.
newsitem.headline: UK wheat futures up, active on shipper buying.

text.p: LIFFE wheat futures firmed today in active trading driven by shipper buying, but eased off highs later in the day, traders said.
Main interest was on May, most traded with 421 lots. Next came Jan with 208. Total volume on wheat was 839 lots.
Some switching out of front month Jan helped to inflate volume, traders said.
Active May last traded up 0.60 stg at 100.60 stg, off a high of 100.80 stg. Front month January last traded 0.55 stg higher at 96.40 stg, just off its earlier high of 96.50.
Barley futures were less active, with front month January last traded 0.25 stg lower at 95.00 stg on 19 lots. Total volume for barley was 33 lots.

Futures traders said that shipper buyers had been joined by domestic grain consumers in the later stages of wheat trading. But, according to a trader at one leading UK feed compounder, end-users are not going to be rushing to buy grain at current prices. "This market has downside rather than upside," he said.

"I can't see this rise continuing, especially with sterling holding its own, or even rising," he said. A likely new-year interest rate rise would further support the UK currency and help grains prices come down, he said.

Compounders still had grain to buy, but they didn't need to follow the market up. Because farmers had, so far, stuck to buying feed on a spot basis, compounders would be able to cover their needs with spot grain.
France still had plenty of grain from the 1997 harvest to sell, and when French farmers started to bring bigger quantities onto the market, prices were likely to be pushed lower.
